title: How Bahrain became Iran’s IRGC pressure point against Washington
author: Giorgio Cafiero

Analysis

How Bahrain became Iran’s IRGC pressure point against Washington

By targeting Bahrain, Iran is seeking to raise the costs of its confrontation with Washington while testing Gulf states’ confidence in US security guarantees.

Giorgio Cafiero

Bahraini police cordon off the area outside the damaged Crown Plaza hotel, following an Iranian military strike, in Manama on March 1, 2026. — Fadhel Madan / AFP via Getty Images

WASHINGTON — Iran renewed its attacks on Bahrain, with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launching a six-drone assault on Nov. 17, four days after a claimed strike on a US early-warning radar facility, marking a sharp escalation after months of relative calm in the Gulf. Missile alerts sounded twice before sunrise on Nov. 18, with explosions reported across the island kingdom as air defense systems engaged incoming threats. Bahraini authorities blamed Iran for the latest attack, the third in a week.Beyond Bahrain’s small size and geographic position, its close military alliance with Washington explains why Iran has repeatedly targeted the country since Feb. 28. The island kingdom hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet headquarters and critical US radar, surveillance and early-warning installations. Tehran considers these facilities legitimate targets because of their role in US military operations.Bahrain as Iran’s Pressure Point Against WashingtonThe latest strikes against Bahrain are intended to demonstrate that US forces and infrastructure in the Middle East cannot be insulated from the consequences of Washington’s pressure on Tehran.
